done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (anything the app's date reader parses, such as last 30 days, explicit dates and date ranges, plus a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: `AMBIGUOUS_MONTH_YEAR_PATTERN` short-circuits all deterministic parsing whenever a month is followed by two digits. This also matches unambiguous app-readable dates such as `since July 25, 2026` and ranges beginning `July 25, 2026 through ...`; the unchanged date reader accepts these forms in `backend/src/chat/timeWindowParse.ts` lines 32 and 105–124. Because `hasTimePeriodWords` then sees the month name, the model window is retained instead of being cleared or overridden. The new test at line 486 even expects the model window for `Jul 25`, although the app's date reader parses that as a month-day date. This violates the required precedence for every period the app reads itself.
findings.title: Not done: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself answers for that period whatever window the model emits

findings.body: The amount guard only recognizes its enumerated link words and therefore still misses ordinary unambiguous amount phrases. For example, in `Show an amount that is 2025`, `AMOUNT_BEFORE_NUMBER_PATTERN` fails because `that` is not an `AMOUNT_LINK`; none of the currency, comparison, or suffix guards apply, so `calendarYear` returns 2025 and replaces the model/prior window with calendar year 2025. `Show an amount that should be 2025` fails similarly. The newly added direct cases such as `amount around 2025` do not cover this remaining violation.
findings.title: Not done: an amount is never read as a year

findings.body: The added matrix calls `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, whose LLM, executor/warehouse, audit, dimensions, reports, and resolver are fakes; the period-control rerun test uses the same fixture. `ask-period.test.ts` is likewise service-level with fake infrastructure. The registered suites contain no Playwright flow through a running frontend, API, real database, and period-control interaction, so named-period precedence, inheritance/aggregation, amount protection, and user-driven reruns still lack the required end-to-end proof. The successful close run exercised only these lower-boundary Node/jsdom suites.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
